reader.requirement: At --std 85, when one character position is described by more than one data description entry (data-name-2 and its redefinitions, and their subordinates), every one of those data-names references that position: a store through any description is seen through every other, for elementary and group views, alphanumeric, numeric DISPLAY (signed, scaled), edited, COMP and COMP-3 descriptions, condition-names under a redefinition, and reference modification, in working-storage and in file records.
reader.edition-search: grep of Edition./CobolVersion/DialectLevel/Has( over ClassifyRedefinesClassesPass.cs, RedefinesModel.cs, PlaceBuilder.cs, ReferenceResolver.cs, CodeGen/Roslyn/PlaceRenderer.cs and CodeGen/DataDivision/PhysicalModel.cs, RecordStructEmitter.cs: only diagnostic Edition.At/Error appear; the one Edition.Has(2002) in ReferenceResolver.cs is the EXCEPTION-OBJECT register test, off this path. A view's place is built the same way at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises alphanumeric and DISPLAY-numeric views inside OCCURS, a group view, ref-mod and an ODO table; not exercised: COMP/COMP-3 views of the same bytes, signed and scaled DISPLAY, edited views, condition-names under a redefinition, several redefinitions of one area, and file records

OK  §1985:VI.5.10.4 GR1  (5.10.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: Every description of a shared area is a window on the one backing (Tier B) or a pass-through of the one field (Tier A), so a store through any name is seen through all. A 0xFF byte read through an alphanumeric view is HIGH-VALUE, held as U+FFFF (ORD 65536, DISPLAY writes EF BF BF): that is the landed design of kb/Work PB1759 (owner R52, a 65,536-character native alphanumeric set), not a REDEFINES defect.
